title: Guided SDK Tutorial Series — Sprint Notes & Quickstart Checklist
content:
TL;DR:
A compact plan + running notes for a 4-week guided SDK tutorial series aimed at new integrators (engineers & platform teams). Objective: ship a single-file Quickstart + three interactive labs + observability homework that reduce time-to-first-success from hours to 20 minutes.

Why this exists (motivation):
- Lots of small SDK docs split across repo and console; newcomers get lost between auth, client setup, and streaming examples.
- We want a single coherent path that engineers can follow in a live workshop or self-serve.
- The deliverables should be copy/paste runnable and produce visible telemetry (so we can measure retention).

Audience:
- Primary: Full-stack engineers integrating Redwood API into product flows (chat, generation, embeddings).
- Secondary: Platform/infra engineers evaluating Dedicated/Private deployment patterns.

High-level goals (metrics):
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) median <= 20 minutes for workshop participants.
- Self-serve completion rate (end-to-end quickstart) >= 40% within 1 week of signup.
- Telemetry: 60% of completions send at least one streaming request and one embedding request.

Series format:
- 4 weekly guided sessions (90 min live or self-paced modules) + 1 optional deep-dive sprint.
- Each session: 15 min context, 45–60 min hands-on lab, 15 min wrap + feedback.
- Deliverables per session: single-file quickstart snippets, small test dataset, evaluation prompt set, telemetry checklist.

Session plan (short):
Week 0 (prework): accounts, API keys, environment setup. Provide a single script to validate env.
Week 1: Hello Redwood — Simple generation end-to-end (client init, sync generate, error modes).
Week 2: Streaming & Tooling — real-time streaming example + function calls stub.
Week 3: Embeddings & Retrieval — vectorize, simple kNN retrieval, cache hints.
Week 4: Production-focused — batching, retries, telemetry, and cost controls + rollout checklist.
Optional deep-dive: Private deploy basics and quantization notes (for infra audiences).

Quickstart (single-file) — design sketch (copyable):
- Filename: quickstart-redwood-onefile.py (or .js)
- Must do: show auth, call, error handling, streaming fallback, simple local retry.
- Minimal Python example (to include in repo):

# quickstart-redwood-onefile.py
import os
import time
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient  # pseudo-client name for illustration

API_KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=API_KEY, timeout=10)

try:
    resp = client.generate(model='redwood-2-small', prompt='Write a 4-line haiku about latency')
    print('RESP:', resp.text)
except Exception as e:
    print('Quickstart error:', e)
    # hint: check env and network proxy

# simple streaming fallback pattern
for chunk in client.stream_generate('redwood-2-small', 'Say hello'):
    print(chunk, end='')

Checklist for Quickstart: (must be visible in README)
- [ ] 1-click run via Docker / Codespaces (devcontainer)
- [ ] Environment validation script that checks connectivity and keys
- [ ] Minimal logging to surface latency and token counts
- [ ] Single README section titled "20-minute quickstart"

Lab design notes (session-by-session):
- Lab 1 (Hello Redwood): include common pitfalls table: AUTH_MISSING, MODEL_UNSUPPORTED, RATE_LIMITED. Quick fixes & links to error docs.
- Lab 2 (Streaming): simulate a flaky network using local proxy script and show how client resumes / falls back to non-streaming.
- Lab 3 (Embeddings): provide 50-row toy dataset and prebuilt metrics notebook to test recall@k.
- Lab 4 (Production): include small CI check that runs smoke generation and checks tokens/unit cost estimate.

Telemetry & gating (implementation):
- Expose three telemetry markers that Quickstart emits (event names): 'qs_start', 'qs_stream_used', 'qs_embed_complete'.
- Hook these into Console demo project so product team can observe completion funnel.
- Slack webhook for workshop runs over threshold (>= 25 participants) to announce success and capture cohort feedback.

Acceptance criteria for "ship":
- Quickstart repo runnable in < 20 steps (ideally 3).
- One passing E2E smoke test in CI that validates auth + generation.
- Telemetry events correctly appear in demo console project.
- Workshop script and facilitator notes ready; two engineers rehearsed.

Open questions / risks:
- What model should be default in snippets? (redwood-2-small vs community open model) — pick the smallest verified model to reduce cost during workshops.
- How much of Console do we surface in Quickstart? Minimal; links to Console for deeper observability.
- Legal: do we need a simplified data policy paragraph in the Quickstart README before demos? Ops to confirm.

Dependencies & owners:
- Client team: must ship a tiny "quickstart" client release with stable import path (owner: Marco).
- Docs: canonical README section + short video (owner: Samir).
- Solutions eng: create workshop slide deck + cohort sign-up (owner: Lena).
- QA: smoke tests and telemetry assertions (owner: Priya).

Immediate next actions (first sprint):
- Create repo skeleton and add single-file quickstart + README (Evelyn -> 1 day).
- Add env-check script and Codespaces devcontainer (Marco -> 3 days).
- Draft workshop facilitator notes and deck (Lena -> 5 days).
- Wire telemetry events with demo console (Samir -> 7 days).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep code minimal; examples that try to be clever end up confusing folks.
- Use explicit prompts, not abstract tasks, for determinism during demos.
- Have backup plan: prerecorded video of run if live demo network fails.

Feedback log (initial):
- 2024-11-18: Marco — prefer JS first examples; include both Python and JS snippets.
- 2024-11-20: Lena — add a quick module on costs and token estimation under "production".
- 2024-11-27: Priya — add a CI check that runs a mocked API if keys are missing.

Unresolved edits to make before publish:
- Inline token usage example for each code sample (estimate tokens and cost).
- Add small GIFs to show streaming vs non-streaming behavior.
- Add short troubleshooting section: common error messages and exact commands to fix.

If you're reading this and want to help: pick one micro-deliverable from "Immediate next actions" and drop a comment with ETA.

End of notes.
